title: Droplet typeface
lede: Hat Nguyen’s family of swollen, irregular display letters for T-26, named as a signature grunge font.
summary: Blobby, irregular sans-serif capitals and lowercase in Lite, Regular, and Extra weights. Hat Nguyen, T-26, 1996.

evidence.note: Inspected the Klingspor Museum specimen sheet for Hat Nguyen (a one-page PDF, rendered at about 900 × 1300) and the Fonts In Use render (779 × 176), in scratchpad copies. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit: sources name it a signature grunge font, but its letters are swollen and irregular rather than eroded or torn.

context: The Awl, quoting T-26 founder Carlos Segura, names Hat Nguyen’s Droplet among the signature grunge fonts distributed by T-26. [The Awl](https://web.archive.org/web/20150925150838/http://www.theawl.com/2012/08/grunge-typography).

The Klingspor Museum sheet lists Droplet Lite, Droplet, and Droplet Extra as 1996 T-26 releases, also sold by Linotype. [Klingspor Museum](http://www.klingspor-museum.de/KlingsporKuenstler/Schriftdesigner/Nguyen/HNguyen.pdf).
T-26 still sells Droplet in four styles: Lite, Regular, Extra, and Closed, tagged “bloated”, “hybrid”, “ink”, and “organic”. [T-26](https://www.t26.com/fonts/253-Droplet).
observed: Droplet Lite is a thin, slightly wobbly sans-serif; Droplet and Droplet Extra are heavy, with swollen terminals and small, irregular counters.
Letter widths and stroke ends vary: the I has a hook, the Z and K are compressed, and the Extra weight’s counters close up into blobs.
Edges are smooth, not speckled or torn.
interpretation: Droplet shows that “grunge font” was also a market label for any irregular, hand-made-looking display face of the mid-1990s. For the eroded core of the style, prefer [Reactor](ref:reactor-typeface-fuse-1993) or [Trixie](ref:ff-trixie-typeface-1991).
borrow: Pair one swollen, irregular display face with a clean text face for a looser, inky mood without heavy damage.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The typeface is by Hat Nguyen and T-26.
